title: Tenant network evolution pathway & prioritization commitment framework
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers request staggered network changes, proxy bridges, and staged upgrades for VPC/on-prem/private installs. Current intake funnels these into broad buckets which delays decisions and causes repeated rework between PM/Eng/Support. Goal: create a lightweight, repeatable prioritization canvas and commitment framework that assigns an operational path (self-serve, concierge, engineering-assisted) and a measurable SLA for each lane. Scope: networking readiness checks, proxy-bridge proposals, OS/kernel upgrade windows, airgap patch sequencing, and rollback plans. Out of scope: pure product feature requests or bug triage unrelated to network constraints. Deliverables: 1) A one-page prioritization canvas that scores requests across Risk, Customer Value, Effort, and Cross-team Dependencies. 2) Three remediation lanes (Self-Serve, Concierge, Engineering-Assisted) with explicit entry criteria and SLA commitments. 3) Communications templates for customer kickoff, preflight failures, and rollback notifications. 4) A small scorebook and handbook for SEs to run the intake during discovery calls.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritization canvas PDF adopted as official intake artifact and linked from intake form
Three remediation lanes documented with entry/exit criteria and sample runbooks
Scorebook reproducible by Solutions Engineers with <= 10 minutes per request
SLA commitments published internally: initial response within 48 hours, remediation lane assignment within 72 hours for high-priority requests
Two pilot customers onboarded through the new flow and feedback logged

notes: Unique aspects: frame prioritization as an operational commitment to customers (we tell them which lane and the expected timeline), reduce back-and-forth by standardizing preflight outputs, and protect engineering by clearly surfacing capability gaps as dependencies. Track pilot metrics: time-to-lane-assignment, remediation success rate, and SE time-per-intake.
